sections.name: General Knowledge / Current Affairs of India and Goa

p1.title: Passage 1
paras: The global agricultural sector faces a massive challenge: it must drastically scale food production to meet a growing population while simultaneously cutting its heavy environmental footprint under the pressures of climate change. The twentieth-century Green Revolution relied on intense inputs—using massive amounts of chemical fertilizers, synthetic pesticides, and groundwater pumping—which damaged soil ecology, depleted aquifers, and accelerated biodiversity loss. Continuing with this resource-heavy paradigm is ecologically impossible. Achieving sustainable food security requires adopting smart agricultural innovations, such as precision farming using IoT sensors, developing climate-resilient crop varieties that resist drought, and scaling agroecological farming systems. However, smallholder farmers, who produce the majority of food in developing countries, are often locked out of these technologies due to high costs and lack of credit. True agricultural resilience requires building equitable technology distribution frameworks, offering localized crop insurance against weather shocks, and protecting seed sovereignty for small farmers.

p2.title: Passage 2
paras: The global transition away from fossil fuels toward a renewable energy matrix is frequently framed as a linear techno-economic evolution, yet it represents an incredibly complex geopolitical and structural bottleneck. While the plummeting levelized cost of solar photovoltaic modules and wind turbines fuels optimism, the inherent intermittency of these green assets exposes the deep inadequacy of legacy electrical grids. Baseload power generation, historically anchored by coal and natural gas, cannot simply be swapped for weather-dependent inputs without triggering severe transmission instability or rolling blackouts. Resolving this structural paralysis requires monumental capital expenditures into utility-scale energy storage systems, smart grid distribution networks, and long-range high-voltage direct current lines. Beyond these engineering hurdles lies a fraught geopolitical landscape; the green transition reshapes global trade dependencies, shifting leverage from petroleum-exporting cartels to nations controlling the extraction and refining of critical minerals like lithium, cobalt, and rare earth elements. Consequently, hasty decarbonization without robust grid orchestration risks triggering severe economic contraction, proving that the energy transition is as much a challenge of geopolitical security as it is of ecological survival.

questions.q: A major negative legacy of the twentieth-century Green Revolution, according to the passage, is
opts: the end of synthetic pesticide manufacturing
deep environmental damage, including degraded soil and depleted aquifers
a drop in food production that triggered famines
over-reliance on decentralised technology for small farmers
questions.why: Second sentence. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: Which is listed as a modern innovation for sustainable food security?
opts: more groundwater pumping with chemical inputs
precision farming with IoT sensors and climate-resilient crop varieties
questions.why: Fourth sentence. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: Smallholder farmers in developing nations struggle to adopt modern agri-tech because of
opts: high technology costs and lack of credit
questions.why: Fifth sentence. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: According to the text, true agricultural resilience requires
opts: shifting all farming to corporate monocultures
fair technology distribution, localised insurance and seed sovereignty
questions.why: Last sentence. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: The author's main argument is that food security must be achieved by
opts: balancing higher production with ecological sustainability and smallholder equity
questions.why: The opening sets the dual goal; the ending adds equity for small farmers. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: The term “intermittency” in the passage refers to the fact that renewable sources
opts: are too expensive for developing economies
depend on the weather and do not give a constant flow of power
are using up lithium and cobalt
questions.why: The next sentence calls them “weather-dependent inputs”. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: Swapping baseload power for renewables without changing the grid results in
opts: severe transmission instability and possible rolling blackouts
an end to oil cartels' leverage
questions.why: Third sentence. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: The green transition alters global geopolitics by
opts: empowering nations that control critical-mineral supply chains
forcing every nation onto HVDC lines
questions.why: Leverage shifts to nations refining lithium, cobalt and rare earths. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: Which is NOT mentioned as a requirement for integrating renewables?
opts: Subsidising domestic coal and gas extraction
questions.why: Only the first three are listed in the fourth sentence. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: The author's view on the speed of decarbonisation is that
opts: it should be accelerated regardless of grid readiness
a rushed transition without grid orchestration can cause economic contraction
it is a simple linear evolution
it will succeed without changing geopolitics
questions.why: Last sentence. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: Identify the error: “She has been studying here since three months.”
questions.why: A period takes 'for'; 'since' needs a point in time. GPSC CBRT, Mar 2026.

questions.q: Choose the correct inversion:
opts: Never I have seen such chaos.
Never have I seen such chaos.
Never I had seen such chaos.
Never did I saw such chaos.
questions.why: Negative adverb first, then auxiliary before the subject. GPSC CBRT, Mar 2026.

questions.q: Choose the correct modal: “You ____ have apologized for your mistake.”
questions.why: 'Should have' + past participle expresses a missed duty. GPSC CBRT, Mar 2026.

questions.q: Choose the correctly spelt word:
questions.why: Double c and double m. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the meaning of the idiom “to burn the midnight oil”:
opts: to work or study late into the night
questions.why: Standard idiom. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: UIDAI launched an SDK and sandbox in September 2026 for AI-based in-app:
questions.why: Aadhaar Face Authentication SDK, for authentication and KYC. Sep 2026.

questions.q: The Supreme Court of India is established under Article:
questions.why: Article 214 provides for High Courts.

questions.q: The BRICS Traditional and Indigenous Sports Demonstration Games 2026 were held in:
World Post Day (9 October) marks the founding of the Universal Postal Union, headquartered at:
questions.why: UPU was founded in 1874.

questions.q: In 2026, Goa hosted the third BIMSTEC Conference on Traditional Medicine, Genetic Resources and:
India test-fired the Agni-4 ballistic missile in August 2026 from:
questions.why: Integrated Test Range, Chandipur.

questions.q: Semicon 2.0, unveiled at SEMICON India 2026, has an outlay of about:
BHASHINI, which signed a Statement of Intent with NITI Aayog in 2026, is a platform for:
The Shanghai Cooperation Organisation, whose 2026 summit was held in Bishkek on its 25th anniversary, was founded in:
questions.why: India became a full member in 2017.

questions.q: The SI unit of electrical resistance is the:
questions.why: Static science.

questions.q: Piky, Quiky and Riky alone finish an assignment in 7, 8 and 11 days. Together they earn 1,105 coins. Find each share.
In a 4,000 m race on a 1,000 m circular track, the fastest runner (twice the slowest's speed) first meets the slowest at the same point after 5 minutes. How long does the fastest take to finish?
questions.why: He gains one lap (1,000 m) in 5 min: v − v/2 = 200, so v = 400 m/min; 4,000 ÷ 400 = 10 min. GPSC CBRT, Jan 2024.

questions.q: The average age of a teacher and three students (all the same age) is 20. The teacher is 20 years older than each student. What is the teacher's age?
questions.why: T + 3S = 80 and T = S + 20, so S = 15 and T = 35. GPSC CBRT, Jan 2024.

questions.q: In a row of 40 students, A is 13th from the left and B is 9th from the right. C is 4th to the left of B. How many students are between A and C?
questions.why: B is 32nd from the left, C is 28th; between 13 and 28 are 14 students. GPSC CBRT, Jun 2025.

questions.q: A woman says, 'I weigh 50 kg plus one third of my weight.' What is her weight?
questions.why: w = 50 + w/3, so w = 75. GPSC CBRT, Jun 2025.

questions.q: Find the odd one out: 3, 5, 11, 14, 17, 21
questions.why: 14 is the only even number. GPSC CBRT, Jun 2025.

questions.q: Choose the word least like the others: Metaphor, Simile, Hyperbole, Allusion, Sonnet
questions.why: A sonnet is a poem form; the others are figures of speech. GPSC CBRT, Jun 2025.

questions.q: Find the wrong number: 1, −4, 9, 16, 25, −36
questions.why: Squares with alternating signs: 1, −4, 9, −16, 25, −36. GPSC CBRT, Jun 2025.

questions.q: If 6 jerseys are given to each player, one player gets only 4. If 4 are given to each, 30 are left over. How many jerseys and players?
questions.why: 6p − 2 = 4p + 30, so p = 16 and jerseys = 94. GPSC CBRT, Jun 2025.

questions.q: A bus travels 160 km in 4 hours and a train 320 km in 5 hours. What is the ratio of distances they cover in one hour?
questions.why: 40 : 64 = 5 : 8. GPSC CBRT, Nov 2023.

questions.q: Hahnemann (§246, sixth edition) allows repetition of the remedy at suitable intervals provided that:
opts: each dose is given unchanged in the same potency
only placebo is given in between
each dose is slightly modified in potency (by succussion) so the vital force does not resist it
the remedy is changed each time
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. The same unchanged dose repeated would provoke reaction.

questions.q: Hahnemann discovered the prophylactic use of Belladonna in:
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. Published in 1801 on scarlet fever.

questions.q: Psoric skin eruptions are typically:
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. Itching is the hallmark of psora.

questions.q: Gastric upset from overeating, with a thick, milky-white coated tongue and a sulky, irritable child who cannot bear to be looked at, suggests:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Antimonium crudum: thick milky-white coated tongue, gastric upset from overeating.

questions.q: Ill effects of fright followed by stupor, painlessness, a dark red face and loud snoring breathing point to:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Opium: ill effects of fright, stupor.

questions.q: Violent delirium with fear of the dark and desire for light and company, and stammering, suggests:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Stramonium: terror, wants light and company.

questions.q: Complaints from loss of vital fluids (haemorrhage, diarrhoea, lactation), with periodicity and great sensitivity to touch, call for:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. China: weakness from loss of fluids.

questions.q: Maceration and percolation are methods used to prepare:
questions.why: Topic 3, Pharmacy. The plant material is soaked (maceration) or extracted by slow filtration of solvent (percolation).

questions.q: The abbreviation 'q.i.d.' on a prescription means:
questions.why: Topic 3, Pharmacy. Quater in die.

questions.q: Clinical repertories differ from general repertories mainly because they:
questions.why: Topic 4, Repertory. Rubrics are named after clinical conditions.

questions.q: The order of evaluation in Kent's method is:
opts: mental generals, physical generals, then particulars
questions.why: Topic 4, Repertory. From the innermost to the outermost.

questions.q: The sciatic nerve arises from the:
questions.why: Topic 5, Anatomy and Physiology. The largest nerve in the body.

questions.q: Surfactant in the lungs is secreted by:
questions.why: Topic 5, Anatomy and Physiology. Its lack causes respiratory distress in preterm babies.

questions.q: Programmed cell death without inflammation is called:
questions.why: Topic 6, Pathology, Microbiology and Diagnostics. Physiological cell death.

questions.q: Hepatitis A is transmitted mainly by the:
questions.why: Topic 6, Pathology, Microbiology and Diagnostics. As is hepatitis E.

questions.q: An elderly patient with a sudden severe headache, 'worst ever', and neck stiffness may have:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Needs urgent CT scanning.

questions.q: Haemorrhoids that bleed and protrude like a bunch of grapes, relieved by cold water, with a sense of insecurity of the rectum, suggest:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Aloe: grape-like piles, cold water relieves, unsure sphincter.

questions.q: Anaemia, chlorosis with flushing of the face on the least emotion, and vomiting of food after eating suggest:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Ferrum met: false plethora, flushes easily.

questions.q: A painless vaginal bleeding in the third trimester most suggests:
questions.why: Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. Abruption is usually painful.

questions.q: Anterior fontanelle normally closes by about:
questions.why: Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. Between 12 and 18 months; delayed in rickets and hypothyroidism.

questions.q: The immediate first aid for a burn is to:
opts: cool the area with clean running water for about 20 minutes
questions.why: Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. Cooling limits tissue damage.

questions.q: Inflammation of the tonsils with sore throat and difficulty in swallowing is:
questions.why: Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. Quinsy is a peritonsillar abscess.

questions.q: Biomedical waste in India is segregated by colour-coded bags. Human anatomical waste goes into the:
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. Yellow category: anatomical, soiled and chemical waste for incineration.

questions.q: Vital statistics include all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. Vital events are births, deaths, marriages, divorces and so on.

questions.q: A doctor may break patient confidentiality without consent when:
opts: there is a legal requirement or a serious risk to others
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. For example, notifiable diseases or a court order.
